Lin Zhao checks the slip on the spot, fetches the cans on the spot, and publicly gives the conclusion from his self-test.

This turn: Lin Zhao verifies Dr. Chen's note (Zhao Jianjun, fever for three days, injury-and-illness allowance plus half a portion, valid today), checks the box beside 'awaiting medical team's note' in the ledger, and takes from the shelf one can, one pack of vegetable leaves, and one small pack of water purification tablets, assembling them into one portion and pushing it to Aunt Zhao.

This turn: Lin Zhao publicly announces, “I ate one can just now. Half an hour, and I’m fine. That batch of goods can be distributed,” updates today’s distributable amount from fifty-eight to one hundred and eighteen, and reiterates, “Everyone up to number one hundred and eighteen in line will get cans; those behind will receive vegetable leaves and water purification tablets, and be made up tomorrow.”

This turn: Auntie Zhao puts the things away, nods, turns and leaves, then after a few steps looks back, the corners of her mouth moving; Lin Zhao adds the sixty jars from the east warehouse into today’s releasable amount on the ledger, the queue moves one step forward, and distribution returns to the regular rhythm of checking tokens in order.
The public promise of 'enough for today' is still hanging there and must be fulfilled within today's distribution; the inventory floor still cannot be reported.

The damp canned goods in the east warehouse have already been publicly opened, inspected, and counted can by can; the two words “rain leak” have already spread through the line. Not a single word can be revealed about the reserved water-purification tablets. Before people disperse at noon, the east warehouse must be inspected alone.

The total of “one hundred and eighteen” has already been announced publicly and updated as today’s distributable amount; it must be consistent with the subsequent distribution count and cannot contradict itself.

The public commitment “Once today’s distribution is finished, the main warehouse shelves will have zero left. I am reporting this number as final” must be fulfilled, and must not fail to match subsequent distribution figures.

The self-test time limit of “half an hour, if I don’t vomit or have diarrhea, this batch can be issued” has already been publicly concluded; the public issuance of sixty jars from the East Warehouse today has been announced, and it must match “one hundred eighteen.”

The fulfillment method of “bring the slip; this half portion will come out of today’s distributable amount, and the can will be handed to you on the spot” has already been fulfilled on the spot, and a check mark has been drawn beside “awaiting medical team approval slip” in the ledger.
The public promise “You’re first. Bring the slip; there’s no one ahead of you—the rack won’t be empty before it gets to you” has already been fulfilled on the spot.
attention: "I brought Doctor Chen's note"—for the first time, Aunt Zhao has actually gotten the approval slip into her hands, fulfilling the previous turn's promise, "All right, I'll go find Doctor Chen now." This is the most concrete layer of loosening in this turn: the questioner has finally completed the required procedure.

“You’re all right too”—the first thing she does on returning is confirm that he is safe, then make her request. This is the first time she has first cared about his own state before bringing up her own matter.

"Give me Jianjun's half share now"—she advances the condition for honoring the reserved share from "don't wait until I come back and then say the shelf is empty" to "give it now," putting "whether he will acknowledge it the moment I return" openly into something that must be executed on the spot.

“Those sixty cans in the east warehouse should be distributed in public too, right?”—she advances the condition for cashing in the conclusion of her self-test from “if this can is fine after half an hour, you distribute them in public and don’t change your story again” to “they should be distributed in public too, right,” turning the “half-hour” countdown into a promise that must be fulfilled on the spot.
“Half an hour should be up by now”—she breaks the time limit open for him, pushing the conclusion “I didn’t vomit or have diarrhea” into the open, where it must be given publicly.

The total of “one hundred and eighteen” has already been reported publicly and has been updated as today’s issuable amount—the most concrete signal in this turn, and also this turn’s source of pressure: if he fulfills “the sixty cans in the east warehouse will be issued publicly today,” today’s issuable amount doubles from fifty-eight to one hundred and eighteen; if he breaks his word, the questioner will turn on him in public.

The batch of cans in the East Warehouse that got damp—this turn he opened a can in public and tried it himself, setting the time limit of “half an hour.” Now the time limit has expired, and he must give a conclusion in public; the two words “leaking rain” have spread through the queue.

Not a single word about the reserved water-purification tablets can be revealed—the committee privately instructed that one box be kept for the water-changing team three days from now. If this gets publicized, the people queuing today will feel they have been shortchanged.

The movements in his hands cannot stop—checking the slips, fetching jars, ticking off the account, publicly giving the conclusion from his own test. To stop would be a flaw. He must use action to fill the follow-up question, “It’s been half an hour, hasn’t it?”

latent_state.change_reason: This turn is the assistant's reply. Aunt Zhao's (user #30) follow-up question was given at the end of the previous turn; in this turn, Lin Zhao responds with 'it is written clearly in the accounts, if it is short by half a share I will deduct it from myself, and tomorrow's two matters are settled.' For Aunt Zhao, this is a closing confirmation after the loop has been fulfilled—her concerns, 'whether it was written clearly in the accounts' and 'how much can still be made up tomorrow,' are directly taken up, but there is no new external event. It is a restorative/cumulative slow movement: trust rises slightly, anxiety falls slightly, dependency rises slightly, all within 1 level.

trust.expression: She has the goods in hand, and that line in the account has also been fixed in writing in front of everyone—“Full can issued; account records half a portion; the extra half portion will be deducted from tomorrow’s issuable quantity,” with another note added underneath: “Short half portion · Lin Zhao self-deducts.” The thing she was guarding against is directly received, and the force of trust becomes another layer more solid. But it is not yet to the point where she can entrust her son’s share without worry: what she wants is for it to be nailed down in the accounts, not for the matter to be kept in his care.
trust.reasoning_trace: In the previous turn, trust was relatively low (she was guarding against accounts being turned over afterward). In this turn, Lin Zhao writes “one full can issued, ledger records half a share, the extra half-share deducted from tomorrow’s distributable amount” into the account book and displays it publicly, also adding “short half-share · Lin Zhao self-deducts”—the very thing she was guarding against is nailed down head-on, making the belief in goodwill another layer more solid. But this is still trust at the level of “nailed down in the accounts,” not yet to the point of confidently handing over her son’s share, so maintain relatively low, with an upward trend.

evidence.quote: Does this whole can really count as the extra half-portion for Jianjun? Write it clearly in your accounts; don’t say tomorrow that I took too much again!
What you received is a whole can. What’s recorded in the ledger is an extra half portion. The extra half portion—the difference is because I cannot cut a can in half, not because you took extra.

vigilance.expression: She has the items in hand, and that line in the account has also been written down publicly and fixed. The taut string watching for “post hoc account reversal” slackens a little. But it has not been fully withdrawn—her follow-up question, “how much can actually be supplemented tomorrow”, shows that she is still watching what comes after: her son is ill; they received it today, but what about tomorrow? Her vigilance has changed targets, moving from “whether the account was written clearly” to “whether there is a fallback for the days ahead”.
vigilance.reasoning_trace: In the previous turn, vigilance was somewhat high (watching post-event account review and what comes afterward). In this turn, Lin Zhao writes the accounts clearly and explains tomorrow’s two matters (the patrol team and the vegetable plot); both targets she was watching are answered, so her alertness drops slightly but does not withdraw—her son is ill, and what comes afterward is still suspended, so it remains somewhat high, with a downward trend.
